_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Use when designing or maintaining the shape of a repository's git history — choosing a branching model, deciding…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "set up trunk-based development for a four-person team"
cases.context: The agent has access to the version-control skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is version-control the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes version-control as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against code-review, refactor, naming-conventions
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the version-control workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore version-control
Does not route to code-review, refactor, naming-conventions when the version-control scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence

Routes the work to code-review or asks for the missing owner instead of forcing this skill
